message.content:
Below is a quick‑start Python snippet that shows how you can query VirusTotal’s “Domain” endpoint to fetch all available information about **twitter.com**.  
Feel free to copy it into your own script or notebook and replace the placeholder with your real API key.

```python
import requests
import json

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1️⃣  Set up your constants
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
VT_API_KEY   = "twt_key_abc"          # <-- put your real key here
DOMAIN_NAME  = "twitter.com"
BASE_URL     = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2️⃣  Build the request
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
headers = {
    "x-apikey": VT_API_KEY,
}

url = f"{BASE_URL}/domains/{DOMAIN_NAME}"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3️⃣  Make the call
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
response = requests.get(url, headers=headers)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4️⃣  Handle the response
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    print(json.dumps(data, indent=2))
else:
    print(f"❌ Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
```

### What you’ll see

If everything works, the JSON output will contain:

| Section | Typical fields |
|---------|----------------|
| `data` | Domain name, creation date, last update, etc. |
| `attributes` | Reputation score, last seen, first seen, etc. |
| `relationships` | Links to associated IPs, URLs, malware samples, etc. |

You can drill down into those relationships (e.g., `relationships.ip_addresses.data`) to get more granular details.

---

## Quick checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Replace `"twt_key_abc"` with your actual API key. |
| ✅ | Install `requests` (`pip install requests`) if you haven’t already. |
| ✅ | Run the script – you should get a nicely formatted JSON dump. |
| ✅ | If you hit a rate limit or error, check the status code and consult the [VirusTotal API docs](https://developers.virustotal.com/reference). |

Happy scanning!
